mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST) below 1.2 million units signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < 1200 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate increase above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer purchasing power and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 98 for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in CPIAUCSL below 2.0% coincident with a federal funds rate cut (FEDFUNDS drops by >0.5pp month-over-month) signals easing inflationary pressure and accommodative policy, which supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS growth > 5% for three consecutive months) signals elevated precautionary behavior by households, which typically precedes a decline in consumption and corporate revenue, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > 5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month indicates a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to absorb new entrants, which compresses wage growth and profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS growth < 0.1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1.5 million units for six consecutive months signals a robust residential construction cycle, which boosts demand for materials and services and supports corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
